verdict.rationale: Kimi is itself an AI assistant with a documented built-in Agent. In Kimi Code Desktop and the CLI the Agent reads code, edits files, runs commands and autonomously completes tasks, and the consumer app offers an Agent task mode, Agent clusters and Agent-built web pages. Community reports of the agent spending many tokens or breaking code concern output quality, not whether delegation exists. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the consumer app's agent mode and its limits (the help entries are only headings), and independent hands-on corroboration of end-to-end delegated tasks.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Open a local project folder in Kimi Code Desktop and let the Agent read code, edit files, run commands, and verify results through conversation.
